facts.fact: The Ministry of Health's Digital Health Roadmap states that DHIS 2 was first implemented as the national HMIS tool in 2008 and that by 2010 the District Health Management Teams had started reporting data directly into a centralised online version.

The Roadmap's landscape assessment states that DHIS 2 and tracker applications are widely used with 96% coverage of public health facilities and no corresponding adoption by private facilities; it gives no numerator or denominator, the figure is coverage and not facilities entering their own reports, and it is undated, so the Roadmap's published year is used.

The Roadmap's table of digital health tools lists DHIS2 as the Health Management Information System, deployed by the MoH in all districts and at the scaled stage, with the DPPI's HMIS Unit responsible for its indicators; undated, so the Roadmap's published year is used.

The National Digital Health Roadmap 2024-2026 sets an objective to strengthen digitisation of the routine HMIS: an in-depth assessment of the national HMIS, a revised HIS strategic plan, and optimising the DHIS 2 deployment on the recommendations of a 2022 maturity assessment, with targets of 10, 50 and 75% of recommendations implemented in 2024 to 2026.

The Roadmap states that eight EMR projects are under way at different stages, and its table lists them at pilot, prototype or pre-implementation stage: among primary facilities, OpenMRS at Wellbody clinic in Kono (pilot), the Facility Management Information System at one PHU each in Kambia and Port Loko (pilot) and Salone EMR at Waterloo PHU (pre-implementation); undated, so the Roadmap's published year is used.

The Roadmap's table names a partner or company as the organisation deploying each EMR: CUAMM Doctors with Africa (Elysium EMR, PCMH), Partners In Health (OpenMRS, Wellbody clinic), GOPA-GIZ (FMIS), GIZ (Salone EMR), UNICEF (OpenMRS, Ola During Children's Hospital), Health Connect (34 Military Hospital, Connaught Hospital) and Sierra Rutile Ltd; it adds that data from deployed tools sits on multiple hosting platforms with limited access by the MoH. Undated, so the Roadmap's published year is used.

facts.fact: The National Digital Health Roadmap 2024-2026 plans a centrally governed, open-source, FHIR-compatible national EHR, expanded in phases to all tertiary and district hospitals and selected PHUs in a hub and spoke model under DPPI, with selected facilities having the EMR deployed to rise from a 5% baseline to 10, 15 and 25% in 2024 to 2026; it also records that draft EMR guidelines written by the MoH in 2020 were not yet validated or published.

The Roadmap names the Ministry of Health's DPPI as responsible for deploying the national EMR, which it says should be centrally governed and reusable across facilities nationwide; undated, so the Roadmap's published year is used.
